rule: UI source -> command -> canonical owner -> validation/permission -> state mutation or operation -> event/receipt/ObservableWork -> UI projection -> Usage/diagnostic attribution -> recovery/deep link
honesty_note: This concept is a prototype. Nothing below is production wiring: local state and seeded receipts stand in for it, and that substitution is stated rather than implied. The traces record what the wiring WOULD have to be.

concept_specific.route_state_machine: explicit: home | query | domain | manager | copy | all, each with an optional state fixture, parsed into a destination object before anything renders
concept_specific.persistence_keys: pm2:concept-05-directory-take-1:v2 — changed values, manager edits, dismissed notices, copy receipts, the active fixture and the last route. In-flight operations are deliberately not persisted.
concept_specific.back_contract: Back moves one Settings level out and names its destination; Escape closes popup, then detail or drawer, then one level out, and stops at Settings Home
concept_specific.narrow_contract: the rail pushes off-screen, the grid becomes one column, roster and form become two pushed pages

traces.validation: the immutable result id must still resolve; an id that no longer exists returns a kept-query notice rather than a guess
traces.effect: route change to the resolved destination object
traces.projection: domain, page, manager, object, section and row selected, focus moved, one calm locator highlight
traces.recovery: Back restores both the query text and the chosen result

traces.validation: type and range check; permission and FileSafe where the value governs tool reach
traces.effect: value written for the current Project at an expected revision
traces.observable: none for a local write; an ObservableWork operation when the value triggers a restart or a probe
traces.projection: row state becomes Changed; the copy preview and All Settings counts move with it
traces.recovery: restore the default; a stale revision surfaces as the changed-elsewhere state rather than a silent overwrite

traces.projection: origin, default, recommendation, restart requirement and availability reason in Details

traces.validation: availability of the manager on this host
traces.effect: lazy hydration of that manager only
traces.observable: hydration is not an operation; any probe it starts is
traces.projection: manager surface inside the same Settings shell, Project, breadcrumb, search, Back and Close retained
traces.recovery: Back returns to the owning domain

traces.owner: BinaryLocator and the shared integration lifecycle
traces.validation: explicit user action, exact host or environment, official source, publisher and architecture verification
traces.effect: installation staged, verified, activated and bound by identity
traces.observable: ObservableWork with named phases and a real denominator only where one exists
traces.projection: installation row moves from not present to in use; shadowed candidates named
traces.recovery: rollback to the previous generation; an unidentifiable owner stays manual-only

traces.validation: source readable, destination writable, preview still current
traces.effect: restore point, then one atomic write of the previewed values, then verification
traces.observable: ObservableWork with a counted denominator, cancellable before commit
traces.projection: receipt with counts and a rollback action; the two Projects remain independent
traces.recovery: verification failure rolls the whole transaction back and says so

traces.effect: hand-off with the originating destination and a continuation token
traces.observable: the owner's own operation, projected read-only in Settings
traces.projection: the owner's surface; Settings keeps the destination that opened it
traces.recovery: the owner returns to the exact Settings destination named in its return contract

traces.validation: the check must currently be failing; a passing check offers no repair
traces.effect: dispatch to the owning subsystem's existing repair command
traces.observable: ObservableWork, with a truthful terminal, degraded or recovery-required state
traces.projection: the check re-runs and reports its own result; Doctor never asserts success on the owner's behalf
traces.recovery: retry, or escalate to the named owner

notifications_and_receipts.inbox: Every simulated operation emits one receipt into the shell's notification inbox through the single PMSim/PMWork path, so an operation can never appear twice or not at all.
notifications_and_receipts.receipt_contents: operation, real call a production build would invoke, outcome word, timestamp, and the rollback action where one exists

unresolved: Whether cmd.settings.copy_from_project.rollback is a new id or a reuse of the restore-point command is a census question, not a design question.
Whether Doctor's repairs dispatch by command id or by a typed capability handle depends on how the owning subsystems already expose repair.
